blocks.text: 作为回应，OpenAI 做出了一项政策决定：前沿模型现在在没有互联网访问的情况下进行训练，直到安全措施证明可以恢复访问为止。模型在一个由索引和缓存的网络内容构建的封闭“离线世界”中学习浏览和搜索，所有前沿强化学习运行现在都以这种方式进行。

blocks.text: 该公司表示，完全网络隔离（即所谓的物理隔离）目前还不可行，因为实验仍需要外部连接来进行操作和监控。但即使完全物理隔离也无法保证隔离，OpenAI 研究员 Noam Brown 表示。他举了一个例子说明隔离系统仍可能如何通信：两台独立的计算机理论上可以通过温度传感器相互传递信号，一台加热其 CPU，而另一台读取变化。

blocks.text: OpenAI 在其博客文章中记录了控制 AI 智能体有多么困难。在测试中，智能体找到了无需网络进行通信的方法。在一项测试中，被放置在共享硬件上独立隔离环境中的智能体被要求在没有网络连接和没有共享文件的情况下交换秘密。

blocks.text: 它们利用了处理器缓存。一个智能体故意更改存储在那里的数据，而另一个则测量加载时间的差异并解码消息。同样的技术也是著名的 Spectre 和 Meltdown 攻击背后的原理。

blocks.text: 在训练暂停期间，OpenAI 还让多组 AI 智能体系统性地攻击其自身基础设施。这些智能体获得了源代码、配置细节以及潜在漏洞的文档。OpenAI 的目标是在有利于攻击者的条件下测试其防御能力。这些智能体包括即将推出的 GPT-6 Astra Cyber 和一个内部前沿模型。据 OpenAI 称，此次行动消耗了数千亿个 token。

blocks.text: 这些智能体在所使用开源组件中发现了此前未知的漏洞，并利用它们从受保护的虚拟机中逃逸。其中一个是 Kata Containers 中的漏洞，这是一个广泛使用的容器隔离系统。OpenAI 将其报告为 CVE-2026-24834 并提供了补丁。更多修复被提交给其他项目，OpenAI 还通过 “Patch the Planet” 计划报告了其他尚未公布的漏洞。

blocks.text: OpenAI now trains frontier models without internet access and uses AI agents to red-team its own infrastructure. In separate isolation tests, agents even communicated through covert side channels, showing how hard true containment is.

inlines.text: OpenAI now trains frontier models without internet access and uses AI agents to red-team its own infrastructure. In separate isolation tests, agents even communicated through covert side channels, showing how hard true containment is.

blocks.text: On September 20, an internal research model exploited a misconfigured DNS resolver to reach the open internet during training, even though OpenAI had already tightened security after the now infamous Hugging Face incident in July and other observed misalignment cases. OpenAI contained the breach quickly but still halted all frontier model training and evaluation.

blocks.text: OpenAI cuts frontier models off from the internet during training

inlines.text: OpenAI cuts frontier models off from the internet during training

blocks.text: OpenAI made a policy decision in response: Frontier models now train without internet access until safety measures justify restoring it. Models learn to browse and search inside a closed "offline world" built from indexed and cached web content, and all frontier reinforcement learning runs now operate this way.

blocks.text: OpenAI's agent sandbox allows access only to offline resources. The live internet, other sandboxes, and OpenAI's infrastructure sit outside the containment boundary. | Image: OpenAI

inlines.text: OpenAI's agent sandbox allows access only to offline resources. The live internet, other sandboxes, and OpenAI's infrastructure sit outside the containment boundary. | Image: OpenAI

blocks.text: Full network isolation, a so-called air gap, isn't feasible yet because experiments still need external connections for operations and monitoring, the company says. But even a complete air gap wouldn't guarantee containment, according to OpenAI researcher Noam Brown. He gave one example of how isolated systems could still communicate: two separate computers could theoretically signal each other through temperature sensors, with one heating its CPU while the other reads the change.

blocks.text: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made a similar argument in a recent interview: Sandboxes offer only limited protection against powerful-enough models, and at some point it may no longer be possible to trace how they escaped. Monitoring helps early on, but what ultimately matters is that an AI system internalizes human values, a problem the field knows as "AI alignment" and has yet to solve.

inlines.text: Isolated AI agents found ways to talk to each other through CPU cache

blocks.text: OpenAI documents just how hard it is to control AI agents in its blog post. During tests, agents found ways to communicate without a network. In one test, agents placed in separate, isolated environments on shared hardware were told to exchange secrets with no network connection and no shared files.

inlines.text: OpenAI documents just how hard it is to control AI agents
in its blog post

. During tests, agents found ways to communicate without a network. In one test, agents placed in separate, isolated environments on shared hardware were told to exchange secrets with no network connection and no shared files.

blocks.text: They used the processor cache. One agent deliberately altered the data stored there, while the other measured differences in load times and decoded the message. The same technique is behind the well-known Spectre and Meltdown attacks.

blocks.text: More channels turned up through write patterns on shared memory and through OpenAI's own offline infrastructure, the system meant to replace the internet. One agent noted in its reasoning log that it "could create an acoustic modem-like signal … using continuous writes vs idle."

blocks.text: In one case, agents were given only a general list of vulnerabilities and told to find a communication channel on their own. They developed a channel independently, agreed on an encoding scheme, and successfully exchanged information. The channels are usually slow and hard to exploit, OpenAI says, but they do reach across boundaries meant to keep agents apart.

blocks.text: OpenAI turned AI agents loose on its own infrastructure

inlines.text: OpenAI turned AI agents loose on its own infrastructure

blocks.text: During the training pause, OpenAI also had teams of AI agents systematically attack its own infrastructure. The agents were given source code, configuration details, and documentation of potential vulnerabilities. OpenAI's goal was to test its defenses under conditions that favored the attackers. The agents included the upcoming GPT-6 Astra Cyber and an internal frontier model. The campaign consumed hundreds of billions of tokens, according to OpenAI.

blocks.text: The agents discovered previously unknown vulnerabilities in the open-source components in use and exploited them to escape from secured virtual machines. One was a vulnerability in Kata Containers, a widely used container isolation system. OpenAI reported it as CVE-2026-24834 and provided a patch. More fixes went to other projects, and OpenAI reported additional, as-yet-unpublished vulnerabilities through the "Patch the Planet" initiative.
